definitions.explanation: A piece of playground equipment consisting of a long plank balanced at its center, on which two people sit at opposite ends and rise and fall alternately. From English "seesaw."

examples.japanese: ⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧シーソー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}った→乗る：00511_noru⟧。
examples.english: I rode the seesaw at the park.

examples.japanese: ⟦{妹|いもうと}→妹：00573_imouto⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧シーソー⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{交互|こうご}→交互：16076_kougo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{上|あ}がっ→上がる：00615_agaru⟧たり⟦{下|さ}がっ→下がる：01188_sagaru⟧たり⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My sister and I went up and down in turns on the seesaw.

examples.japanese: ⟦{体重|たいじゅう}→体重：03395_taijuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、シーソー⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦うまく→うまい：01279_umai⟧⟦{釣|つ}り{合|あ}わない→釣り合う：14468_tsuriau⟧。
examples.english: When the weights differ, a seesaw doesn't balance well.

notes:
A common piece of playground equipment, alongside ⟦{滑|すべ}り{台|だい}→滑り台：06325_suberidai⟧ (slide) and ⟦ぶらんこ→ぶらんこ：06324_buranko⟧ (swing). The word is also used figuratively for things that go alternately up and down, as in シーソーゲーム (a back-and-forth, see-sawing contest).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- シーソー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧: to ride a seesaw
- シーソー⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧: to play on a seesaw
- シーソーゲーム: a see-saw game (a closely contested, back-and-forth match)
